name: howto
title: Fill a tire with a cordless inflator in five minutes
sub: The number to use is on the door placard, not on the tire
footer: Sources: NHTSA tire-safety guidance (via search summaries, October 2026); Milwaukee and DeWalt manuals. Always follow your pump's manual.

items.head: Check tires cold
items.body: Before driving, or after the car has sat for three hours. Warm tires read 4–6 psi high.

items.head: Find the placard number
items.body: Door-edge label or owner's manual. The sidewall figure is the tire's maximum, not your target.

items.head: Charge or fit the battery
items.body: Built-in batteries: charge first. Tool-only pumps need a charged 18V/20V or 12V pack.

items.head: Screw on the chuck
items.body: Thread the hose onto the valve fast and fully; a hiss means it is not seated.

items.head: Set the target and start
items.body: Dial in the placard psi. Auto-stop shuts the motor off at that number.

items.head: Verify and rest the pump
items.body: Confirm with a handheld gauge, then let the pump cool: Milwaukee asks for 40 minutes after 20 of use.
